findings.fix_hint: add shutdown_drain_timeout to save_settings' general dict (from the form with a 1.0..3600.0 clamp, or carried through from current_settings.general like tracking_delay_seconds)
findings.problem: The new GeneralConfig field is a persisted config value. However, save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:539-551) rebuilds the whole `general` dict from a fixed key list and does not include shutdown_drain_timeout. It does carry other fields through, for example `tracking_delay_seconds: current_settings.general.tracking_delay_seconds`. So when a user sets a drain timeout in config.toml, the next save from the settings UI writes the TOML without it, and the value silently falls back to the 60.0 default. The comment in the diff also mentions a 'form clamp (3600.0)', but no such form handling exists in routes.py. pending: confirm a later plan in phase 75 adds the field to the save_settings dict or the form.
findings.title: Saving settings silently resets shutdown_drain_timeout to 60.0
findings.why_it_matters: A configured shutdown drain timeout is quietly lost on any unrelated settings save. Shutdown then uses a value the operator did not choose.

findings.fix_hint: have _read_shutdown_drain_timeout take settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout as the default and call it at shutdown time instead of at import
findings.problem: The comment says 'Config value is the default; TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env overrides at shutdown'. In fact triggarr/search/scheduler.py:81 still computes _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT once at import from the env var alone, and lines 611-656 use that constant. Nothing reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout, so changing the config value has no effect on the drain. pending: confirm whether the scheduler wiring is planned in a later 75-xx plan rather than meant to ship with this change.
findings.title: Config field is never read; scheduler still uses the env-only module constant
findings.why_it_matters: Operators who set the value in config get no change in behavior, which contradicts the comment.

agent_notes: Consistent with the existing pattern: the bounded Field(...) with a tag-prefixed rationale comment matches max_consecutive_failures (SAFETY-03) on line 134. The design spec states this intent directly ('same defensive intent as max_consecutive_failures's bounds').

The spec as written (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-recovery-counts-config-design.md) says Field(default=60.0, ge=1.0). The diff adds allow_inf_nan=False. That goes beyond the spec, is justified by the test in tests/test_config.py:192-197, and is not a design deviation.

Dead-field window: until scheduler.py reads settings.general.shutdown_drain_timeout instead of the import-time _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT constant (used at lines 611-656), the field has no effect at runtime. The spec's implementation note says the read must move to scheduler-construction or shutdown time where settings is available. Tests in tests/test_scheduler.py:629-678 import and monkeypatch the module constant directly, so the refactor will need to update them.

Cross-lane note for bugs/security: the existing env-var reader _read_shutdown_drain_timeout (scheduler.py:70-75) accepts 'inf' and 'nan'. max(nan, 1.0) returns nan, and max(inf, 1.0) returns inf. Under the planned precedence, the env var beats the finite-only config value, so the env path needs math.isfinite as well. This code is outside the diff, so it is not a finding here.

Cross-lane note for compliance: CLAUDE.md requires Pydantic validation before any config write. This diff adds the field to the model, so validation will cover it once the settings form writes it. The routes.py form handler (around line 548, which uses safe_int clamps) does not handle the field yet, which is expected in a later commit.
No import cycles, new dependencies, cross-module reach-ins or duplication introduced. The diff is a single model field.

agent_notes: Blast radius: the change is one additive field with a default on GeneralConfig. Many modules import models/config.py (about 9 in production code, 19 test files), but none of them construct GeneralConfig with positional args or require that its key set stay fixed. No public API signature changed.

Schema/migration: none. Existing config.toml files without the key load with the 60.0 default. After any UI save, model_dump (routes.py:227) writes `shutdown_drain_timeout = 60.0` into the TOML file. That is harmless, but operators will see a new key show up.

Main risk is ordering inside phase 75: save_settings (routes.py:539-550) does not carry the field forward, so a hand-edited value is lost on the next UI save. Also, scheduler.py still uses the env-only module constant read at import (scheduler.py:81, 634, 648), so the field does nothing yet. Both look like planned later tasks (form clamp 3600.0, scheduler refactor), but they must land before release.
Performance: none. The field is read once per config load and validation cost is trivial.

Cross-process: the drain timeout only matters at shutdown. A wrong value there means either SIGKILL during the drain (if the drain outlasts Docker's stop_grace_period of 90s) or a shortened drain. Note that a configured value above about 85s exceeds the documented stop_grace_period: 90s, and Docker will SIGKILL before the drain finishes. That interaction belongs in the release notes once the UI ceiling (3600) ships.

Verdict: safe as an intermediate step. Before shipping, wire the field into save_settings and the scheduler shutdown path, or UI saves will silently revert the setting and the setting will have no effect.
